title: Nuclear structure and notation; Decay law and half-life; Mass defect and binding energy; Fission and reactors; Fusion
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: N01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; N01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; N01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; N03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N01-1#N.3, N03-1#N.2, N03-uk1#N.13, N04-1#N.3b, N05-1#N.2b, N05-uk1#N.4, N06-1#N.2b, N01-1#N.5, N03-1#N.5a, N04-1#N.6, N05-1#N.5, N05-uk1#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Nucleon number
items.clue: Symbol A: the total count of protons plus neutrons, 56 for iron-56.

items.label: Proton number
items.clue: Symbol Z: it fixes which element an atom is, 26 for every iron atom.

items.label: Neutron number
items.clue: Found as A – Z: 30 for iron-56, and 6, 7 or 8 for the three forms of carbon.

items.label: Decay constant
items.clue: Symbol λ, unit s⁻¹: the probability per unit time that a nucleus breaks down.

questions.stem: A nucleus of potassium-40 is written in nuclear notation as ⁴⁰₁₉K. Which statement about this nucleus is correct?

options.text: It contains 40 neutrons.
It contains 19 neutrons.
It contains 19 nucleons.
It contains 21 neutrons.

questions.stem: Predict first. Radioactive decay is described as random and spontaneous. Which statement correctly describes what this means?

options.text: A nucleus decays when a collision or a rise in temperature gives it the energy it needs.
Nuclei decay roughly in the order in which they formed, but their ages cannot be known.
The count rate varies so unpredictably that the half-life of a sample cannot be measured.
When a given nucleus decays cannot be predicted, and outside conditions do not alter its chance.

questions.stem: A hospital technician checks a short-lived medical tracer. She plots ln(activity / MBq) against time t in hours. The best-fit straight line falls from 6.0 at t = 0 to 4.6 at t = 6.0 h. What is the half-life of the tracer?

Radium-226 decays by α emission: ²²⁶₈₈Ra → ²²²₈₆Rn + ⁴₂α. The atomic masses are 226.025410 u for radium-226, 222.017578 u for radon-222 and 4.002603 u for helium-4 (the electron masses cancel). Take 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg = 931.5 MeV c⁻², 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. How much energy is released in the decay of one radium-226 nucleus?

Some very heavy nuclides, such as californium-252, can undergo spontaneous fission, whereas uranium-235 in a reactor undergoes neutron-induced fission. Which statement about spontaneous fission is correct?

options.text: Energy is released as kinetic energy of an α particle that breaks off the nucleus.
Energy is released only once the material is hot enough for its nuclei to shake apart.
No energy is released, as no neutron has been absorbed to supply the energy.
Energy is released when the nucleus splits into two fragments of comparable mass.

questions.stem: A reactor is running at a steady power. The operators want to raise its power output slightly and then hold it at the new level. What should they do with the control rods?

options.text: Withdraw them slightly, then reset them once the new power is reached.
Push them further in, so they soak up more heat and the fuel can run hotter.
Withdraw them fully, since the reactor can give more power only with no rods in.
Leave them alone and pump the coolant faster, since the coolant sets the fission rate.

questions.explanation: Fewer neutrons are absorbed, so for a while each fission leads to slightly more than one further fission and the power rises. Then the rods are reset so that exactly one does, and the power holds steady.

questions.stem: In the fusion reaction ²₁H + ³₁H → ⁴₂He + ¹₀n, the binding energies per nucleon are 1.11 MeV for ²₁H, 2.83 MeV for ³₁H and 7.07 MeV for ⁴₂He. A free neutron has no binding energy. How much energy is released in one reaction?

options.text: 10.7 MeV
17.6 MeV
28.3 MeV
3.13 MeV

questions.stem: Predict first. Carbon-12 (¹²₆C) and carbon-14 (¹⁴₆C) are isotopes of carbon. Which statement about these two nuclides is correct?

options.text: They contain the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.
Both contain the same number of protons, but different numbers of neutrons.
Their atoms have different chemical properties, as their nuclei differ.
Their nuclei are identical, but their atoms have different numbers of electrons.

questions.stem: A hospital prepares a dose of technetium-99m (half-life 6.0 h) that has an activity of 800 MBq at 08:00. What will its activity be at 14:00 the next day?

options.text: 0 MBq
160 MBq
25 MBq
12.5 MBq

questions.stem: Predict first. Which statement correctly describes the binding energy of a nucleus?

options.text: The energy released when the nucleus is separated completely into its nucleons.
The energy stored inside the nucleus, which it gives out when it later decays.
The minimum energy needed to pull the nucleus apart into separate nucleons.
The energy equivalent of the extra mass a nucleus has over its separate nucleons.

questions.stem: A uranium-235 nucleus absorbs a neutron and splits into two fragments and 2 free neutrons. The fragments contain 234 nucleons in total. The binding energy per nucleon is 7.6 MeV for uranium-235 and about 8.5 MeV for the fragments. A free neutron has no binding energy. Roughly how much energy is released?

options.text: 0.9 MeV
2.0 × 10² MeV
2.0 × 10³ MeV
1.8 × 10³ MeV

questions.explanation: Energy released = increase in total binding energy = 234 × 8.5 − 235 × 7.6 = 1989 − 1786 ≈ 200 MeV.

questions.stem: Two radioactive isotopes in spent fuel start with the same activity. Isotope P has a half-life of 30 years; isotope Q has a half-life of 24 000 years. Which statement about storing them is correct?

options.text: P needs secure storage for longer, because it decays faster and so stays more active.
Q needs secure storage for far longer, because its activity falls only very slowly.
Both need storage for the same time, because they start with the same activity.
Neither needs long storage, because both have decayed completely after two half-lives.
